examples: Please add some green onion to the soup.
I bought a bunch of green onion at the mart.
I sliced the green onion finely and put it on top.
nuance: 대파 is the thick long green onion used in almost every Korean soup and stew, sold by the 단 (bunch). The thin small kind is 쪽파, so do not mix them up at the market.
mistakes: Confusing 대파 with 양파 (onion)
Counting 대파 with 개 instead of 단

examples: I added more chili powder to the kimchi stew.
It is not spicy because there is no chili powder.
Do not add too much chili powder.
nuance: 고춧가루 is the dried red chili powder that gives Korean food its red color and heat, and the spelling has the ㅅ (사이시옷) between 고추 and 가루. It is coarser than Western cayenne and used by the spoonful in stews and kimchi.
mistakes: Writing 고추가루 without the ㅅ
Confusing 고춧가루 with 고추장 (chili paste)

examples: I drizzled oil in the pan and fried an egg.
The cooking oil ran out, so I have to buy some.
Deep-frying uses a lot of cooking oil.
nuance: 식용유 is the everyday neutral frying oil (usually soybean or canola), as opposed to flavoring oils like 참기름 or 들기름 that you add at the end. You drizzle it with the verb 두르다 rather than 넣다.
mistakes: Using 식용유 when you mean sesame oil 참기름
Saying 식용유를 넣다 instead of 두르다 for coating a pan

usage: I season it with perilla oil
examples: Seasoned greens taste good tossed with perilla oil.
Perilla oil goes bad fast, so keep it in the fridge.
I lightly brushed perilla oil on the seaweed.
nuance: 들기름 has a strong nutty, earthy aroma and is used for namul and seaweed, while 참기름 (sesame oil) is lighter and more common. It oxidizes quickly, so Koreans keep it refrigerated and use it in small amounts.
mistakes: Confusing 들기름 with 참기름 (sesame oil)
Storing 들기름 at room temperature so it goes rancid

examples: I sprinkled sesame salt over the greens.
You just add sesame salt at the end.
It tastes nuttier thanks to the sesame salt.
nuance: 깨소금 is toasted sesame seeds ground with a little salt, used as a finishing seasoning sprinkled on namul and other side dishes. In everyday speech people also loosely call plain toasted sesame seeds 깨소금.
mistakes: Thinking 깨소금 is just salt rather than sesame plus salt
Adding 깨소금 early instead of as a finishing touch

examples: Adding a little ginger removes the fishy smell.
I had a cold, so I drank ginger tea.
Ginger has a strong aroma, so add just a little.
nuance: 생강 is fresh ginger root, used in small amounts to cut fishy smells in meat and fish and brewed as 생강차 for colds. It has a sharp pungent kick, so recipes usually call for only a little.
mistakes: Confusing 생강 with 마늘 (garlic) in a recipe
Adding too much 생강 because the flavor is strong

examples: 다시마를 넣고 물을 끓여서 육수를 냈어요.
I made broth by boiling water with kelp.
Take the kelp out before it boils.
I steeped broth from anchovies and kelp.
nuance: 다시마 is dried kelp used as the base for Korean soup stock, usually together with 멸치 (dried anchovies). A key tip: pull it out right before the water boils, or the broth turns slimy and bitter.
mistakes: Confusing 다시마 (kelp) with 미역 (wakame)
Letting 다시마 boil too long so the broth gets bitter

examples: I made anchovy broth and cooked soup.
이 집은 육수가 정말 진하고 깊어요.
This place has really rich, deep broth.
If the broth is short, add more water.
nuance: 육수 is the savory stock that forms the base of soups, stews, and noodle dishes, made by simmering anchovies, kelp, or bones. Koreans judge a soup mainly by how good its 육수 is, often praising it as 진하다 (rich) or 시원하다 (clean-tasting).
mistakes: Confusing 육수 (broth) with 국물 which is the liquid already in a dish
Assuming 육수 always means meat stock

examples: 두부 한 모 사서 된장찌개에 넣었어요.
I bought a block of tofu and put it in the soybean stew.
두부를 노릇하게 부쳐서 간장에 찍어 먹어요.
I pan-fry tofu golden and dip it in soy sauce.
Soft tofu is much softer than regular tofu.
nuance: 두부 is sold in firm blocks counted with the unit 모, and the softer 순두부 (silken tofu) is used for the spicy stew 순두부찌개. Note the verb for pan-frying tofu is 부치다, the same verb used for jeon.
mistakes: Counting 두부 with 개 instead of 모
Confusing firm 두부 with 순두부 (silken tofu)

examples: I lightly boiled the bean sprouts and seasoned them.
Bean sprout soup is the best for a hangover.
콩나물 한 봉지에 천 원밖에 안 해요.
A bag of bean sprouts is only a thousand won.
nuance: 콩나물 are the long yellow-headed soybean sprouts, distinct from the shorter 숙주 (mung bean sprouts). They are a cheap staple for the side dish 콩나물무침 and the hangover soup 콩나물국.
mistakes: Confusing 콩나물 (soybean sprouts) with 숙주 (mung bean sprouts)
Overcooking 콩나물 so it loses its crunch

examples: Please fry the jeon until golden-brown.
The fish grilled up nicely golden-brown.
nuance: 노릇노릇 is a mimetic word for the appetizing golden-brown color of food that is fried or grilled just right, used with 굽다, 부치다, or 익다. It is almost always positive, signaling the food is cooked to a perfect crispy color.
mistakes: Using 노릇노릇 for burnt food, which should be 탔다
Writing 노룻노룻 instead of 노릇노릇
